trial_court: Second Additional Principal Judge of the Family Court, Jabalpur in Civil Suit No.259-A/2015
case_name: Smt. Dipika Shukla vs Ashish Shukla
facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife. Their marriage was solemnized on 6.2.2006. The wife left the house with their son Vinayak on 1.6.2008. The husband filed a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, which was granted by the trial court. The wife appealed against this order.

legal_principles.principle: Institution of a criminal case alone does not constitute cruelty for the parties seeking divorce unless it is held by the Court that the said complaint/allegation was false and vexatious.
legal_principles.held: The matter is still pending before the Court, therefore, it cannot be said that the false report was lodged by the wife to the police.
cited_cases: Bhola Kumar Vs. Seema Devi, (2015) Patna 119

legal_principles.principle: A dispute related to the operation of a bank locker is not necessarily an act of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The position is clear from the aforesaid three letters that the locker was in the name of the aforesaid three persons. Because the wife was living separately from her husband, therefore, dispute related to the operation of locker was natural.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment of the trial court is set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on irretrievable breakdown of marriage
